new_scholarship.description: Dartmouth College meets 100% of the demonstrated need of all admitted financial aid applicants, regardless of citizenship or entry round, and its financial aid packages never include a required student loan. Need is calculated as cost of attendance minus family contribution, with direct expenses of tuition, fees, food and housing and indirect expenses such as travel, books, supplies and laundry. Families with total annual income below $125,000 with typical assets can expect no parent contribution, while families earning between $125,000 and $175,000 with typical assets can expect a scholarship or grants covering the full cost of tuition. International applicants file the CSS Profile with school code 3351, or the International Student Financial Aid Application if the CSS fee is a serious hardship. Financial aid deadlines are November 1 for Early Decision and February 1 for Regular Decision.

new_scholarship.description: The Aga Khan Foundation's International Scholarship Programme, established in 1969 by His Highness the Aga Khan IV, supports outstanding scholars from selected countries who have no other means of financing postgraduate study, and has supported more than 1,500 students. Awards are made through a global, annual competitive process with a limited number of new awards each cycle. Each award is structured as half grant and half loan, and the recipient must repay 50 percent of the award amount with a guarantor co-signing the agreement; repayment, including a service charge, begins six months after graduation, termination of studies, or withdrawal of support for failing academic standards. The award covers tuition expenses and student living expenses, but not international travel, clothing, furniture or family living expenses. Master's funding runs for the full degree; PhD funding covers the first two years. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed and the next opens in early 2027.

new_scholarship.notes: Rotary awards up to 170 funded fellowships a year across eight peace centers. Since 2002 the program has trained more than 1,900 fellows who now work in over 140 countries, many in governments, NGOs, education and research institutions, peacekeeping and law enforcement agencies, and organizations such as the United Nations and the World Bank. Master's programmes last 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study. The certificate programme is a one-year blended learning option for working professionals who complete field studies and design and carry out a social change initiative. Rotary Peace Fellowships may not be used for doctoral study.
new_scholarship.description: The Rotary Peace Fellowship is funded by The Rotary Foundation and awards up to 170 fellowships a year for leaders with work experience in peace and development to study at one of eight Rotary Peace Centers. Each year up to 50 fellowships fund master's degrees and up to 120 fund professional development certificate studies at partner universities. Fellowships cover tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip transportation, and internship and field-study expenses. Master's programmes run 15 to 24 months and include a self-designed two- to three-month field study, while the certificate programme is a one-year blended learning course for working professionals that includes field studies and a social change initiative. Fellowships cannot be used for doctoral study. Applications open in February and the global deadline is 15 May; the 2027-28 cycle is closed and the 2028-29 cycle opens in February 2027.
